articles.title: Beyond the Fracture Clinic: 3 Things a Surgeon Can Do to Help Older Patients Stay Out of the Hospital.
articles.authors: Ziebart C, Heckman G, Giangregorio LM, Jiwa F, Thain J
articles.population: Older adults aged 60 years and above undergoing orthopaedic surgery
articles.outcomes: Hospital admission rates, falls, fragility fractures, surgical outcomes, intrinsic capacity (locomotion, vitality, cognition, sensory function, psychological well-being)
articles.take_home: Orthopaedic surgeons can help older patients stay healthy and avoid hospital readmission by prescribing muscle strengthening and balance training, screening for malnutrition and supporting good nutrition, and optimising bone health. These three simple interventions can reduce falls and fractures and improve recovery after surgery.

articles.title: Early mortality prediction of prognosis in cardiac arrest patients using machine learning: Development, external validation, and explainability with SHAP.
articles.authors: Sun Y, Wang L, You H, Liu X, Ren J, Wu Y, et al.
articles.study_type: Machine learning model development and validation study
articles.population: Cardiac arrest patients in intensive care units
articles.sample_size: 1749 patients from MIMIC-IV database; external validation using eICU database
articles.outcomes: In-hospital mortality prediction; XGBoost model achieved AUC of 0.8486 in internal validation and 0.8471 in external validation
articles.take_home: Researchers developed a computer model that can predict which cardiac arrest patients are more likely to die during their hospital stay, with good accuracy. The model is now available as an online calculator for clinicians to use.

articles.title: Femoroacetabular stabilization using a suspensory fixation device in post-traumatic hip instability after hip fracture-dislocation: technique and report of 6 cases.
articles.authors: Kung JE, Pumilia CA, Harrison P, Stirling B, Cunningham DJ, Murr K, et al.
articles.population: Patients with residual hip instability after complex hip fracture-dislocation
articles.outcomes: Hip joint stability maintained after femoroacetabular suspension device deployment; avoidance of postreconstruction immobilisation or complex reconstructive procedures
articles.take_home: A suspensory fixation device placed across the hip joint can help keep the hip stable in patients with persistent instability after complex hip dislocations, potentially avoiding the need for prolonged immobilisation or more extensive surgery.

articles.title: Distal Radial Fracture as an Early Marker of Bone Fragility: A Population-Based Study in Japan.
articles.authors: Shibata R, Sato Y, Tanaka Y
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study with propensity score matching
articles.population: Adults aged 65 to 89 years in Japan
articles.outcomes: All-cause mortality, secondary fragility fractures (particularly hip fractures), hospitalisation, long-term care deterioration, and osteoporosis treatment initiation
articles.take_home: Distal radial fractures in older adults may indicate skeletal fragility rather than severe frailty, and represent an opportunity to start osteoporosis treatment to prevent further fractures. Patients with a distal radial fracture had higher rates of subsequent hip fractures and were more likely to receive osteoporosis treatment.

articles.title: Physiotherapist-led care for musculoskeletal conditions in the emergency department (RESHAP-ED): a randomised controlled trial with economic evaluation.
articles.authors: Sigera C, Campos TF, Coombs DM, Williams CM, Rogan E, Edwards J, et al.
articles.study_type: Randomised controlled trial with economic evaluation
articles.population: Adults aged 18 years and older presenting to emergency departments with uncomplicated musculoskeletal conditions such as soft tissue injuries, neck and back pain, and fractures or dislocations not requiring orthopaedic review or surgery
articles.outcomes: Primary outcome: length of stay in emergency department. Secondary outcomes: adverse events and cost-effectiveness
articles.take_home: Physiotherapist-led care reduced emergency department stay by about 1 hour compared to usual doctor or nurse practitioner care, without increasing harm or costs. The physiotherapist approach was also cost-effective and appears safe for uncomplicated musculoskeletal injuries.

articles.title: Expanding the indications of horizontal plate fixation to the proximal humerus: Technical note and clinical series.
articles.authors: Machado JKS, da Silva Cordeiro R, Dos Santos DR
articles.study_type: Technical note with retrospective case series
articles.population: Patients with isolated greater tuberosity fractures of the proximal humerus
articles.outcomes: Fracture union achieved in all patients; mean UCLA Shoulder Rating Scale score of 30; most patients reported mild or occasional pain and minimal functional limitation
articles.take_home: Horizontal plate fixation is a feasible technique for treating greater tuberosity fractures, with all patients in this series achieving bone healing and good functional results. Most patients experienced only mild pain and minimal limitations in shoulder function.

articles.title: An ethnographic study of mobilization, basic mobility, physical activity, and exercise during acute hospitalization in patients following hip fracture surgery.
articles.authors: Hansen MS, Hoite MES, Bandholm T, Lindholm ST, Skibdal KM, Pedersen MM, et al.
articles.population: Patients hospitalized following hip fracture surgery
articles.sample_size: 22 observations, 23 interviews with healthcare professionals and management
articles.outcomes: Mobilization, basic mobility, physical activity and exercise practices during acute hospitalization; identification of barriers to implementing guidelines
articles.take_home: Despite guidelines recommending frequent mobilization after hip fracture surgery, practice varies widely because healthcare teams have different understandings of patient mobility needs, unclear responsibilities, and face challenges including poor communication, limited resources and hospital environments that keep patients in bed. Better coordination between different healthcare professionals and clearer definitions of roles could help improve patient recovery.

articles.title: Fixation of Zone 2 Sacral Fractures Utilizing a Novel Compressive Bolt - A Biomechanical Comparison.
articles.authors: Froerer DL, Jenson S, Gregersen CS, Achebe C, Haller J
articles.study_type: Biomechanical laboratory study using synthetic bone models
articles.population: Standardised synthetic pelvic models with zone 2 sacral fractures
articles.sample_size: 12 Sawbones pelvic models (6 cannulated screw, 6 compression bolt)
articles.outcomes: Sacral fracture gap formation, rotational displacement in three planes, construct completion rate, and consistency of fixation
articles.take_home: In laboratory testing, a new compression bolt fixation method performed better than standard screws for zone 2 sacral fractures, showing less gap opening, less tilting movement, and more reliable fixation. The compression bolt completed all tests whilst one screw failed during testing.

articles.title: Effect of Perioperative Tranexamic Acid on Blood Loss in Posterior Acetabular Fracture Fixation.
articles.authors: Yeager MT, Rutz RW, Dekle JK, Alcaide DM, Litten RM, McIlwain RN, et al.
articles.population: Adult patients undergoing posterior approach acetabular fracture fixation at a single Level I trauma centre
articles.sample_size: 591 patients (186 receiving tranexamic acid, 405 not receiving tranexamic acid)
articles.outcomes: Total blood loss, transfusion requirements, hospital length of stay, postoperative haemoglobin levels, and postoperative complications including infection and blood clots
articles.take_home: Tranexamic acid did not reduce blood loss or transfusion needs in patients having acetabular fracture surgery through a posterior approach. Instead, longer operation time and the specific characteristics of the fracture itself were more important factors affecting blood loss.

articles.title: Limited clinical utility of risk stratification for CT decision-making in patients >/= 75 years with mild traumatic brain injury.
articles.authors: Carbajo S, Barrenetxea I, Luco G, Garaizar I, Garcia-Fontela B, Garrido I, et al.
articles.population: Patients aged 14 years and older presenting to emergency department with mild traumatic brain injury
articles.outcomes: Presence of acute intracranial lesion on head CT scan; model discrimination and potential CT utilisation reduction
articles.take_home: In patients aged 75 and over with mild head injury, risk assessment tools cannot safely reduce CT scans because the risk of missing serious brain injury is too high. Even the best-performing model could only safely avoid about 1 in 67 CT scans whilst detecting all injuries.

articles.title: Trends, disparities, and outcomes of pediatric firearm-related injuries in the United States: A national analysis from 2016 to 2021.
articles.authors: Balian J, Kwon OJ, Tabibian D, Porter G, Tabibian K, Chaturvedi A, et al.
articles.population: Children and adolescents under 18 years old hospitalised with firearm-related injuries in the United States
articles.outcomes: Annual hospitalisation rates and in-hospital mortality; factors associated with hospitalisation outcomes by injury intent and demographic characteristics
articles.take_home: Paediatric firearm hospitalisations increased by over half between 2016 and 2021, with unintentional injuries becoming more common than assault-related injuries. Deaths from these injuries also increased, and the burden fell disproportionately on racial minority children and those from lower-income families.

articles.title: An epidemiological evaluation of fatal and nonfatal assault related firearm injuries among youth aged 0-17 years.
articles.authors: Gilani N, Hunter AA, Lazzarini Z, DiVietro S
articles.population: Children and youth aged 0-17 years in the United States
articles.sample_size: Estimated 6820 nonfatal firearm assaults and over 2300 fatal firearm assaults over two years (2019-2020)
articles.outcomes: Rates of nonfatal and fatal firearm-related assaults; disproportionality and disparity by race, ethnicity, age and gender
articles.take_home: Over 9000 children in the US experienced firearm assault injury or death over two years, with non-Hispanic Black male and older youth experiencing the greatest burden. The researchers call for community violence reduction programmes and policy reform to prevent these injuries.

articles.title: Transformation into chronic subdural hematoma following acute subdural hematoma: Incidence, outcomes, and predictors.
articles.authors: Chen H, McIntyre MK, Santdasani S, Lakhani DA, Malhotra A, Kan P, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using national readmissions database
articles.population: Adult patients aged 18 years and over hospitalised with acute subdural haematoma
articles.sample_size: 189,905 patients (113,942 in training cohort; 37,983 in validation cohort)
articles.outcomes: Incidence of chronic subdural haematoma readmission within 180 days (2.8%); functional decline (26.0% of those readmitted); surgical intervention required (33.6%); mortality (4.3%); median readmission cost £71,474
articles.take_home: About 1 in 36 patients with acute subdural haematoma develop chronic subdural haematoma requiring readmission within 6 months, with significant risk of disability and need for further surgery. A new risk prediction tool called PERSIST can identify high-risk patients who may need closer monitoring.

articles.title: Association of CT-derived adipose measurements with prolonged intensive care unit stay in moderate and severe trauma patients.
articles.authors: Zander C, Muhlenfeld N, Erdle B, Scheef T, Rau A, Reisert M, et al.
articles.population: Moderate and severe trauma patients admitted to a level-1 trauma centre
articles.sample_size: 142 ICU survivors (200 patients initially identified, with exclusions for poor imaging, no ICU stay, and in-hospital death)
articles.outcomes: Intensive care unit length of stay and duration of mechanical ventilation
articles.take_home: CT scans that measure different types of abdominal fat (visceral and subcutaneous) were better predictors of how long trauma patients stayed in intensive care and needed breathing support than traditional weight-based measures. This suggests that detailed fat measurements from routine CT scans could help doctors better assess risk in seriously injured patients.

articles.title: Chloral hydrate outperforms oral midazolam in facilitating venipuncture in children: A double-blind randomized trial.
articles.authors: Khakshour A, Akhondian J, Saeidinia A, Nirooman S
articles.population: Children aged 1-5 years requiring venipuncture in emergency and trauma care
articles.outcomes: Primary: number of venipuncture attempts. Secondary: sedation time, venipuncture duration, total procedural time, recovery time, parent and nurse satisfaction, adverse events.
articles.take_home: Chloral hydrate worked better than midazolam for helping young children stay still during blood tests, requiring fewer needle attempts and taking less time overall. Both medicines were safe, but children and staff were more satisfied with chloral hydrate.

articles.title: Algorithm for the hemodynamically unstable patient with pelvic fracture - The Parkland experience.
articles.authors: Halvachizadeh S, Carron CJ, Katzir A, Sun J, Zhang A, Grewal I, et al.
articles.population: Adult patients with unstable pelvic ring injuries treated surgically at a Level I trauma centre
articles.outcomes: Time to definitive pelvic ring fixation, haemorrhage-control interventions, fixation strategy, complications, and length of hospital stay
articles.take_home: When a trauma centre has immediate access to interventional radiology, patients with life-threatening pelvic fractures can be treated effectively without routine emergency packing, using angioembolization when needed. The timing and type of surgery can be guided by the fracture pattern itself rather than the patient's initial shock state.

articles.title: Prospective analysis of 1619 alpine skiing and snowboarding injuries: Spatial clustering and prevention implications.
articles.authors: Puls L, Wolfsperger F, Ruedin C, Kalin J, Lanter L, Alebrand F, et al.
articles.population: Injured alpine skiers and snowboarders presenting to emergency department at a Swiss ski resort
articles.sample_size: 1619 participants (1190 skiers, 429 snowboarders) over two winter seasons (2022-2024)
articles.outcomes: Injury types and patterns by sex, age, sport type and terrain; spatial clustering of accidents; associations with environmental and terrain factors
articles.take_home: One-third of skiing and snowboarding injuries happened on just 3% of slopes, mostly on steep, narrow, busy runs. Injury types differed by sex and age, such as female skiers getting more knee injuries and snowboarding children getting more wrist fractures, suggesting prevention should focus on slope design changes and sport-specific protective equipment rather than weather conditions.

articles.title: Prophylactic antibiotic use and infectious complications in open pelvic fractures with concomitant visceral injury.
articles.authors: Gochi AM, Patel S, Mathur T, Perez HO, Perez AH, Heximer A, et al.
articles.population: Adult trauma patients aged over 16 years with open pelvic fractures
articles.outcomes: Surgical site infections (superficial, deep and organ space), osteomyelitis, and prolonged antibiotic use (over 72 hours)
articles.take_home: Doctors used many different antibiotic combinations for open pelvic fractures, particularly when patients had injuries to bowel or urinary organs, but using antibiotics for longer or using stronger antibiotics did not reduce infection rates. Patients needing blood transfusions or those with bowel injuries had higher rates of deep infections regardless of antibiotic choice.

articles.title: Professional obstacles: A perception-based survey of women members of AO trauma - Latin America.
articles.authors: Medina C, Arroyo-Berezowsky C, Oberlohr V, Amaral A, Calcado I, Gelvez AG, et al.
articles.population: Women orthopaedic surgeons who are current or former members of AO Trauma Latin America
articles.outcomes: Perceptions of support, inclusion, equality, and barriers to career advancement; variations in perceived inclusion and faculty opportunities between countries
articles.take_home: Most women orthopaedic surgeons in Latin America felt supported and included in AO Trauma, though experiences varied significantly between countries. The survey highlights the need for strategies to increase diversity in orthopaedic trauma surgery in Latin America and globally.
